Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
520 AM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Hot and dry today.

- A cold front will bring a chance for a few showers and
  thunderstorms Saturday afternoon/evening through very early
  Sunday. 
 
- Next week's outlook features seasonably hot and humid conditions
  with isolated afternoon showers and storms possible.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1200 AM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Texas remains in the grip of a strong mid/upper ridge centered over 
New Mexico. However, one can see signs of flux in the pattern by 
taking a gander at the water vapor imagery. Over the northern 
plains, there is a robust mid/upper disturbances that is trending 
from a strong shortwave trough to a more longer wave system. As 
ridging retrogrades into W CONUS this weekend, the aforementioned 
trough should help shift lower mid/upper heights westward in the 
central CONUS, eroding the ridge over Texas. The mid/upper system 
will also foment LL cyclogenesis, resulting in a sfc low that tracks 
across the Midwest this weekend. The low will have a trailing cold 
front that pushes into southeast Texas by Saturday afternoon or 
night. What do all these factors entail for our weather here in SE 
TX? 

The dry and hot regime will continue today. Inland afternoon highs 
in the upper 90s will be common once again, with a few areas 
reaching 100 degrees. Sufficient mixing should keep peak heating dew 
points low enough to prevent widespread heat indices reaching or 
exceeding 108F (Heat Advisory criteria). That being said, various 
locations did briefly reaching 108-109F on Thursday, so I suspect 
that will happen again today. Remember that normal Texas heat is 
dangerous. Today's temperatures should be a tad hotter than normal. 

The trailing cold front approaches the region on Saturday. The exact 
timing of the front will be crucial regarding convection and 
temperatures. LL frontal convergence may already be sufficient to 
initiate at least shallow convection along and ahead of the front. 
But moisture / thermodynamic profiles could allow for deep 
convection, especially if these forcings are able to interact with 
peak daytime heating. A front that waits until Saturday evening / 
night will have less day time heating to play with, while a Saturday 
afternoon FROPA will obviously have more. Couldn't rule out an 
isolated stronger thunderstorm if the timing works out. Saturday's 
temperatures are expected to be in the mid/upper 90s. But with a 
veering LL wind profile and enough sunshine ahead of the front, I 
couldn't rule out temperatures trying to spike up to around 100 
degrees in our central and southern counties ahead of the front. 

Interestingly, guidance has trended towards a somewhat stronger 
front, featuring much lower dew points in its wake. How far south 
this dry air extends is uncertain. But it appears dew points as low 
as the 50s could make it into our northern zones, while dew points 
well down into the 60s could push all the way to I-10. If the 
front's associated showers/storms/clouds are able to clear, yielding 
a bright, sunny Sunday with low dew points and light northerly flow, 
then it's possible my mid/upper 90s temps on Sunday are a little 
low. But I'll stick with mid/upper 90s for now. 

The outlook for next week continues to look seasonably miserable, 
with highs in the mid/upper 90s, isolated diurnal showers/storms, 
and heat indices well over 100 degrees. 

Self 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 520 AM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

VFR conditions continue to persist, but some isolated reduced
visibilities/ceilings remain possible through 15Z especially CXO
and northward along with LBX. The morning will start
out with southwesterly winds around 7-10 kt, then becoming 
southerly in the afternoon with wind speeds around 10-12 kt. 
Can't rule out occasional wind gusts of 15-20 kt. Just after the
current TAF period, will be monitoring for isolated to scattered 
shower/storm development along and ahead of a frontal boundary.

Batiste

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1145 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Light to moderate SW winds should continue through Friday and into
Saturday. By Saturday afternoon and evening, SW winds are expected
to increase somewhat, possibly reaching up to 20 knots sustained
at times. This may result in a modest increase in seas. The 
chance of showers and thunderstorms increases late Saturday 
afternoon and evening as well. By Sunday into Monday, winds may
become westerly. Light to moderate S to SW winds return for
Tuesday and Wednesday.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
1227 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, MARINE, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat continues through Saturday with afternoon highs in 
the mid to upper 90s and maximum heat indices of 102-109F.

- A weak frontal boundary will move through the region Saturday
  night into Sunday bringing a 30-60% chance of rain. Some 
  slightly drier air may work into the region Sunday, but both 
  high and low temperatures will remain largely unchanged. 

- A few, diurnally driven, afternoon thunderstorms are expected to
  develop each day next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This evening through next Thursday)
Issued at 1213 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Friday afternoon surface analysis shows weak high pressure over the 
northern Gulf while a frontal system is in the Plains. Aloft, 
ridging extends from the Pacific coast to the Southern Plains, while 
a shortwave trough is moving into the Great Lakes region. Ridging 
aloft will bring about another hot and dry afternoon today, with 
highs reaching into the mid to upper 90s. A few spots, particularly 
along the coast, may touch heat advisory criteria briefly this 
afternoon, but overall heat indices should top out in the mid-100s.

Moving into the weekend, upper level ridging begins to retrograde 
westward tonight into tomorrow, while the aforementioned shortwave 
trough dives southeast across the Midwest and evolves into a broader 
scale trough over the E CONUS by early Sunday. The evolution of this 
upper trough will give a surface front/low pressure system a push 
south across the Plains and into the lower MS Valley over the 
weekend. This boundary is expected to make its way into the Ark-La-
Tex tomorrow afternoon and to the coast by Sunday morning. While 
this will mean very little for us temperature wise, with highs still 
reaching into the mid-90s both Sat and Sun, it will bring a bit of 
slightly drier air with a brief north/northwest wind shift along 
with a small chance for showers and storms late Sat into Sun. 

Any repreive from the dog days of summer that this front is able 
to bring will be short lived, with SW/S surface winds returning on
Monday as the front becomes increasingly washed out overhead 
through early next week. At the same time, upper level troughing 
will begin to weaken and retreat northward, losing its hold over 
the E CONUS by late Monday. In its wake, broad flat ridging will 
again build across the southern CONUS. With somewhat weak ridging 
overhead, a few afternoon diurnally driven showers and storms will
be possible each day next week, but coverage will be fairly
isolated to widely scattered at best. With little day to day 
change in the synoptic pattern next week, afternoon highs will 
generally range from the mid to upper 90s each day with overnight 
lows in the mid to upper 70s. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1213 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Scattered cloud deck around 3000-4000ft will continue to stream
across the region through the afternoon, while winds remain mainly
W to SW around 10kts. Tonight, winds relax while skies become
mostly clear apart from some high clouds. Tomorrow, winds
strengthen a bit through mid-morning with gusts around 15-20kts
expected into the afternoon ahead of a weak boundary that will
drop into the region tomorrow night.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1213 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Light southwesterly winds and low seas will continue through 
tonight. A weak boundary will approach from the north tomorrow, 
before moving through the coastal waters early Sunday. As this 
boundary approaches it will tighten the pressure gradient slightly, 
allowing winds to increase to around 15kts with gusts to around 
20kts throughout tomorrow. By Sat night into Sun winds increase a 
bit further with sustained 15-20kts and gusts to 20-25kts. The 
boundary will also increase thunderstorm chances late Sat through 
Sun. An exercise caution statement has been issued for tomorrow, and 
a SCA may briefly be needed Sat night/Sun morning. Light southerly 
flow becomes reestablished Monday through the rest of the week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1213 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Hot and humid conditions will continue through Saturday. Rain 
chances will increase Saturday night into Sunday as an upper level 
trough and weak frontal boundary approach the area. A brief period 
of northwesterly winds are expected Sunday bringing some slightly 
drier air into the region. Minimum RH's Sunday afternoon are 
expected to be in the 35-50% range. Winds will turn back out of the 
south Sunday night into Monday. Isolated afternoon thunderstorms 
will develop each day next week.

&&
